title: Canonical completion comparison for finite-colength algebra inclusions
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $f:A\hookrightarrow C$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative rings making $C$ a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Write $M=C/f(A)$ for the quotient as an $A$-module and assume it has a finite filtration of length $r\ge0$ with simple successive quotients (nonzero modules with no proper nonzero submodule). Write the completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] as
$$\widehat A=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m^n,\qquad\widehat C=\varprojlim_n C/\mathfrak m^nC,\qquad\widehat M=\varprojlim_n M/\mathfrak m^nM.$$
Let $\iota_A,\iota_C,\iota_M$ be the natural completion maps and $\widehat f:\widehat A\to\widehat C$ the map induced by $f$. Then $\mathfrak m^rM=0$, the tower defining $\widehat M$ is constant with identity transition maps from stage $r$ onwards, and $\iota_M:M\to\widehat M$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. The map $\widehat f$ is injective and the completed quotient map gives a short exact sequence of $A$-modules
$$0\longrightarrow\widehat A\xrightarrow{\widehat f}\widehat C\longrightarrow\widehat M\longrightarrow0.$$
The canonical map
$$M\longrightarrow\widehat C/\widehat f(\widehat A),\qquad c+f(A)\longmapsto\iota_C(c)+\widehat f(\widehat A)$$
is an $A$-linear isomorphism, whose composite with the quotient isomorphism $\widehat C/\widehat f(\widehat A)\to\widehat M$ equals $\iota_M$. Here both quotients are module quotients, not quotients by ideals. With tensor products denoting extension of scalars [def-weil-module-base-change], the canonical map
$$\widehat A\otimes_A C\longrightarrow\widehat C,\qquad a\otimes c\longmapsto\widehat f(a)\iota_C(c)$$
is an isomorphism of $\widehat A$-algebras; its composite with the tensor flip identifies $C\otimes_A\widehat A$ with the same algebra, and these maps respect the displayed structural inclusion of $\widehat A$.

proof.text: Write the assumed filtration as $0=M_0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\subset M_r=M$. Step 1 applied to $M_i/M_{i-1}$ gives $\mathfrak mM_i\subseteq M_{i-1}$. Repeating these inclusions gives $\mathfrak m^jM_r\subseteq M_{r-j}$ for $0\le j\le r$, and in particular $\mathfrak m^rM=0$. For $r=0$ the filtration already says $M=0$, and the same formula holds.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), part (9): filtration argument for its finite-length quotient

proof.text: Consequently $\mathfrak m^nM=0$ for $n\ge r$, so the canonical identifications $M/\mathfrak m^nM=M$ turn every transition in this tail into the identity. A compatible family is uniquely determined by its coordinate at $N=\max(1,r)$: its later coordinates equal this element of $M$, and each earlier coordinate is its reduction. Conversely the reductions of any $x\in M$ form this family. Evaluation at $N$ is therefore the $A$-linear inverse to $\iota_M$. This also treats $r=0$, when all coordinates are zero. The compatible-family convention is that of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], extended to the displayed module quotients.

proof.text: Let $q:C\to M$ be the module quotient map. The sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}C\xrightarrow{q}M\to0$ is exact by injectivity of $f$ and the definition of $M$. All three modules are finite: $1$ generates $A$, the hypothesis gives generators of $C$, and their images generate $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] with $I=\mathfrak m$. Its Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses hold, and its coordinatewise maps are precisely $\widehat f$ and $\widehat q$. It gives injectivity of $\widehat f$, surjectivity of $\widehat q$, and $\ker\widehat q=\widehat f(\widehat A)$, hence the asserted short exact sequence.

Put $H=\widehat f(\widehat A)$. Step 4 makes $\beta:\widehat C/H\to\widehat M$, $z+H\mapsto\widehat q(z)$, bijective: surjectivity follows from that of $\widehat q$, and a zero value means exactly $z\in H$. Define $\alpha:M\to\widehat C/H$ by the formula in the statement. It is well-defined because replacing $c$ by $c+f(a)$ changes $\iota_C(c)$ by $\widehat f(\iota_A(a))\in H$. Both maps are $A$-linear, and at every coordinate $\widehat q(\iota_C(c))=\iota_M(q(c))$. Thus $\beta\alpha=\iota_M$; since $\beta$ and $\iota_M$ are bijective, $\alpha$ is bijective. These are additive module quotients; no assertion that $f(A)$ or $H$ is an ideal is used.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), part (9), with canonical maps checked using the compatible-family definitions

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] to $I=\mathfrak m$ and the finite $A$-module $P=C$. It gives the bijective $\widehat A$-linear map $T:\widehat A\otimes_A C\to\widehat C$, $a\otimes c\mapsto a\cdot\iota_C(c)$. At coordinate $n$ the scalar action is multiplication by $f(a_n)$ in $C/\mathfrak m^nC$, so $a\cdot\iota_C(c)=\widehat f(a)\iota_C(c)$. The tensor product here uses extension of scalars [def-weil-module-base-change].

Coordinatewise multiplication makes $\widehat f$ and $\iota_C$ ring maps. On pure tensors,
$$T((a\otimes c)(b\otimes d))=\widehat f(ab)\iota_C(cd)=T(a\otimes c)T(b\otimes d).$$
Distributing finite sums of pure tensors proves multiplicativity for arbitrary elements. Also $T(1\otimes1)=1$ and $T(a\otimes1)=\widehat f(a)$, proving that the bijective map of step 6 is an isomorphism of $\widehat A$-algebras with exactly the required structural map. The tensor flip sends $c\otimes a$ to $a\otimes c$; its inverse interchanges the factors again, and the pure-tensor product formula shows that both maps preserve multiplication and the $\widehat A$-structure. Its composite with $T$ therefore gives the stated comparison for $C\otimes_A\widehat A$.
